decisions.what: Canonical topology: bridge -> one monolithic in-amp (or discrete 2-op-amp equivalent) -> REF pin sets the output pedestal -> single-ended output. No discrete front-end op-amp ahead of the in-amp in any shipped vendor reference design.
decisions.why: TI drives the bridge straight into an INA333 with REF from a precision reference and a single RG gain resistor; TI's Analog Engineer's Circuit builds the same shape from two op-amps but the topology (bridge -> diff-amp -> REF-biased output) is identical.
decisions.source: TI TIDUB00 'Single-Supply Strain Gauge in a Bridge Configuration Reference Design' s2-3, Fig.2/A-1 (ti.com/lit/pdf/tidub00); TI SBOA247A 'Single-Supply Strain Gauge Bridge Amplifier Circuit' p1 (ti.com/lit/pdf/sboa247)

decisions.what: A resistor from the bridge's low side to ground (or a matched pair) both limits bridge current and centers the in-amp's input common-mode inside its linear range. Not optional in any cited design.
decisions.why: TIDUB00 uses R4=0/R5=1.27k to hold Vcm at ~2.4V for max output swing ('Vcm of 1.5V to 3.5V produces the largest possible output voltage swing'); SBOA247 design notes 3/6 state R8/R9 'set the common-mode voltage ... and limit the current through the bridge'; INA333 Fig.35 shows the same series-R pattern explicitly 'for low-voltage operation'. bb-amp's bridge already sits at ~1.65V CM by its own excitation/ground design (Q1), so this board doesn't need the resistor to CREATE the CM point, but still needs deliberate current/CM control per the same mechanism.
decisions.source: TI TIDUB00 s3.3, Fig.3 (ti.com/lit/pdf/tidub00); TI SBOA247A design notes 3,6 (ti.com/lit/pdf/sboa247); TI INA333 datasheet Fig.35 'Single-Supply Bridge Amplifier' (ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina333.pdf)

decisions.what: Gain is set by one external resistor for a classic monolithic in-amp (G=1+100k/RG) or two ratio-matched resistors for an indirect-current-feedback (ICF) part (G=1+R2/R1) - a separate resistor pair from, with different matching rules than, any REF-divider pair.
decisions.source: TI INA333 datasheet, gain equation (ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina333.pdf); Analog Devices AD8237 datasheet, 'Setting the Gain', Table 7 (analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8237.pdf)
decisions.why: Different in-amp architectures use structurally different gain-setting networks; conflating the ICF gain pair with a REF-divider pair (which has its own matching requirement) is a plausible schematic error.

decisions.what: Classic (3-op-amp-derived) monolithic in-amps: the REF pin MUST be driven from a low-impedance source. Stated as an operating requirement, not a suggestion, identically across two independent TI parts.
decisions.why: INA333 Pin Functions: 'This pin must be driven by low impedance or connected to ground.' Section 8.2: 'This connection must be low-impedance to assure good common-mode rejection. Although 15 ohm or less of stray resistance can be tolerated ... small stray resistances of tens of ohms in series with the REF pin can cause noticeable degradation in CMRR.' INA828 Pin Functions: 'This pin must be driven by a low impedance source' (its own REF R_IN=40k describes the pin's own input impedance, not the tolerable external source impedance).
decisions.source: TI INA333 datasheet SBOS445C, Pin Functions table + s8.2 (ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina333.pdf); TI INA828 datasheet SBOS792A, Pin Functions table + Reference Input spec (ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina828.pdf)

decisions.what: Indirect-current-feedback (ICF) in-amps: REF is high-impedance by construction and a bare resistor divider does NOT degrade CMRR; gain-setting resistors are adjusted to compensate for any fixed added resistance instead.
decisions.why: AD8237 'Using the Reference Pin' (verbatim): 'Traditional instrumentation amplifier architectures require the reference pin to be driven with a low impedance source. In these traditional architectures, impedance at the reference pin degrades both CMRR and gain accuracy. With the AD8237 architecture, resistance at the reference pin has no effect on CMRR.' Spec table confirms the mechanism: REF differential/common-mode impedance is specified at the same 100 Mohm||5pF / 800 Mohm||10pF level as the signal inputs (footnote: valid for REF/FB pair as well as +IN/-IN) - orders of magnitude above the tens-of-ohms figure that perturbs a classic REF.
decisions.source: Analog Devices AD8237 datasheet Rev.0, 'Using the Reference Pin' section + Specifications table footnote 1 (analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8237.pdf)

decisions.what: Cross-checked, two vendors, full text read: TI's classic-derived in-amp family (INA333, INA828) states the low-Z REF requirement in near-identical wording; ADI's ICF family (AD8237, same architecture as AD8420) states the opposite for its own topology and explains the mechanism (REF/FB compared inside the loop at matched common-mode via the ALS technique, not summed through an external divider). This decides whether bb-amp needs a second active part: a classic in-amp needs an active low-Z REF driver (buffer op-amp, or a reference IC as in TIDUB00's REF5025) to set the ~0.1V pedestal, likely justifying a second active part; an ICF part needs only a resistor divider off 3.3V.
decisions.why: This is the single architecture choice that determines a scope-relevant fork (a second active part or not) at `block-only` - flagged for P2 to decide and record which mechanism it is using, per requirements.md s9a.
decisions.source: TI INA333 + INA828 datasheets (as above); Analog Devices AD8237 datasheet 'Using the Reference Pin' (as above); corroborated only, not load-bearing: ADI technical article 'Drive the REF Pin of New Generation Instrumentation and Current-Sense Amplifiers Without an Op Amp' (analog.com, retrieved as search-engine paraphrase only - MAX4194 classic vs MAX9922 ICF comparison)

decisions.what: Board math restated: 1% droop at 1kHz on a single real pole puts the -3dB corner at ~7kHz; at gain 150-165 that needs roughly 1MHz of gain-bandwidth product in the gain path.
decisions.why: Direct arithmetic from the board's own DC-to-1kHz-flat-within-1% spec and ~150-165 V/V gain (requirements.md s9a); this is the number every candidate part/topology below is checked against.

decisions.what: The lowest-power zero-drift/chopper in-amp (INA333-class) is disqualified by bandwidth, not by precision, at this gain.
decisions.why: INA333 Frequency Response: BW(-3dB) = 150kHz at G=1, 35kHz at G=10, 3.5kHz at G=100, 350Hz at G=1000 - at G~150-165 this is well under half the 7kHz target, before any design margin. Yet its DC precision is exactly what this board wants: Features list states 'Low Drift: 0.1 uV/degC, G>=100', which over a 0-50degC span is only ~5uV - roughly the board's entire ~5uV RTI error budget (requirements.md s9a) by itself, before CMRR and noise are added. This is the central part-selection tension for this block: the part with the wanted drift lacks the needed bandwidth.
decisions.source: TI INA333 datasheet SBOS445C, Features list + Electrical Characteristics 'Frequency Response' table (ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina333.pdf)

decisions.what: An ICF zero-drift part (AD8237-class) gets close to the bandwidth target but is marginal at this exact gain, and only after a bandwidth-mode pin is correctly strapped.
decisions.why: AD8237 'Architecture': 'For gains >= 10, the bandwidth mode pin (BW) can be tied to +VS ... increase the gain bandwidth product of the amplifier to 1 MHz. Otherwise, connect BW to -VS for a 200 kHz [GBW].' Table 2 (high-bandwidth mode) gives 100kHz@G=10, 10kHz@G=100, 1kHz@G=1000 (~1MHz GBW, self-consistent); interpolating to G~150-165 gives roughly 6-6.7kHz - under the 7kHz target with zero margin, and only achieved if BW is strapped to +VS (the wrong strap gives ~5x worse bandwidth). AD8237 also chops internally (~27kHz ALS clock), so not all zero-drift parts are inherently low-bandwidth, but chopping brings a separate ripple footgun (see errata).
decisions.source: Analog Devices AD8237 datasheet Rev.0, 'Architecture' + Table 2 Dynamic Response (analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8237.pdf)

decisions.what: A non-zero-drift, wideband precision in-amp (INA828-class) clears the bandwidth target with large margin but may consume the drift budget alone.
decisions.why: INA828 Frequency Response: BW(-3dB) = 2.0MHz@G=1, 640kHz@G=10, 260kHz@G=100, 33kHz@G=1000; interpolating to G~150-165 gives roughly 160-180kHz, >20x the 7kHz target. But input-stage offset drift is specified at 0.5uV/degC typ - over 0-50degC that alone is ~25uV, roughly 5x the board's whole ~5uV RTI budget. TI's own bridge reference design anticipates exactly this fork (s7.3 'Modifications - Amplifier'): 'Other instrumentation amplifiers can be used to measure the differential bridge voltage, such as, the INA188 for a low drift solution, the INA827 for applications that require a higher bandwidth, or the INA122 for a lower power solution with higher gain.' Whether INA828-class drift is acceptable once P2 runs the full RSS/calibration budget is not resolved here - see OPEN.
decisions.source: TI INA828 datasheet SBOS792A, Electrical Characteristics 'Frequency Response' + 'Voltage Offset' tables (ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina828.pdf); TI TIDUB00 s7.3 'Modifications - Amplifier' (ti.com/lit/pdf/tidub00)

decisions.what: When one in-amp cannot deliver both drift and bandwidth, vendors split the gain across two stages with MOST of the gain in the first (precision) stage, and inject the REF pedestal at the LATER (gain) stage rather than the front end.
decisions.why: TI's cascading app note gives the rule with an equation: two-stage output offset Voso = Vosi1*(GA1*GA2) + Vosi2*GA2 (Eq.3) - 'the Vosi of the first op amp is amplified by the gain of the entire system. The Vosi of the second op amp is amplified only by the gain of the second stage.' Its stated rule of thumb: 'design for most of the gain to be applied in the first stage of the amplifier circuit. This technique ensures that most of the output noise and Voso is due to the first op amp stage, with minimal contributions from later stages.' Quantified by its own Monte Carlo comparison (same 1000V/V total gain, second stage using a device with 100x worse offset than the first): input-referred offset standard deviation grows from 5.15uV (G1=200,G2=5) to 25.06uV (G1=10,G2=100) as gain shifts toward the back stage - roughly 5x worse for identical total gain. Where the pedestal goes: SBOA247's worked 2-stage bridge circuit injects Vref at the SECOND (gain) stage through a ratio-matched resistor network (design note 7: 'R1 must equal R3 and R2 must equal R4' to avoid degrading CMRR), keeping the pedestal off the limited-swing first stage.
decisions.source: TI SBOA356 'Cascading Precision Op Amp Stages for Optimal AC and DC Performance', s5-7, Eq.3, Table 7-1 (ti.com/lit/pdf/sboa356); TI SBOA247A design note 7 (ti.com/lit/pdf/sboa247)

decisions.what: Unresolved tension, flagged not closed: the 'most gain up front' rule (protects drift) directly fights BW=GBW/Gain for a zero-drift front end, since more front-end gain eats the front end's own bandwidth first. Two vendor-shown escapes exist: (a) a non-chopper high-GBW part takes most of the gain in stage 1 (accepts the drift risk of that part class), or (b) a zero-drift part takes only modest front-end gain, keeping its own bandwidth comfortably over 7kHz, with the remaining gain in stage 2 (a smaller drift penalty, scaled by 1/GA1).
decisions.why: This is a P2 sizing decision requiring a specific chosen part pair; this research surfaces the tradeoff and its governing equation but does not resolve it, per this block's scope (topology, not part selection).
decisions.source: DERIVED from TI SBOA356 Eq.3/rule-of-thumb combined with the BW=GBW/Gain relation stated in the same document s3 (ti.com/lit/pdf/sboa356)

decisions.what: A DC return path for input bias current is REQUIRED by every cited in-amp datasheet, not optional conditioning - it is in scope at `block-only`.
decisions.why: INA333 s8.2.2.5: 'The input impedance ... is extremely high - approximately 100 Gohm. However, a path must be provided for the input bias current of both inputs ... Without a bias current path, the inputs float to a potential that exceeds the common-mode range ... and the amplifiers will saturate.' AD8237 'Input Bias Current Return Path': 'The input bias current ... must have a return path to ground. When the source ... cannot provide a return current path, create one.' bb-amp's J1 3rd pole (GND, tied to the bridge's own excitation return per Q2) IS that return path - both vendor sources confirm the brief's own reasoning was correct and not optional.
decisions.source: TI INA333 datasheet s8.2.2.5 + Fig.34 (ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina333.pdf); Analog Devices AD8237 datasheet 'Input Bias Current Return Path' + Fig.74 (analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8237.pdf)

decisions.what: RFI/EMI input RC filtering is OPTIONAL conditioning for parts that already filter on-chip; only becomes relevant if the chosen part lacks on-chip filtering.
decisions.why: INA333 s10.1: 'the INA333 device has been specifically designed to minimize susceptibility to RFI by incorporating passive RC filters with an 8-MHz corner frequency at the VIN+ and VIN- inputs. As a result, the INA333 device demonstrates remarkably low sensitivity.' AD8237: 'contains an on-chip RFI filter that is sufficient for a majority of applications. For applications where additional radio frequency immunity is needed, an external RFI filter can also be applied' with exact equations f_diff=1/(2*pi*R*(2Cd+Cc)), f_cm=1/(2*pi*R*Cc), worked values R=10k 1%, Cc=1nF 5%, Cd=10nF. Both bb-amp's likely candidate families already carry sufficient on-chip filtering, so an ADDED external RC network is conditioning the datasheet does not require for correct operation and stays out of `block-only` scope by default.
decisions.source: TI INA333 datasheet s10.1 (ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina333.pdf); Analog Devices AD8237 datasheet 'Filtering Radio Frequency Interference' + Fig.69 (analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8237.pdf); corroboration only (search-paraphrase, not full text): Analog Devices AD8221 datasheet RFI-filter section, R*Cc mismatch / Cd~10x Cc mitigation rule (analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8221.pdf)

decisions.what: Series input protection resistors are OPTIONAL and explicitly conditional in both cited datasheets, not a blanket requirement - and bb-amp's actual source does not meet either datasheet's trigger condition for adding them.
decisions.why: INA333 s8.2.2.10: 'If the input signal voltage can exceed the power supplies by more than 0.3 V, the input signal current should be limited to less than 10 mA ... Some signal sources are inherently current-limited and do not require limiting resistors.' AD8237 'Input Protection' gives the same conditionality with a sizing formula, R_protect > (Vin-Vs)/5mA, only 'if the application requires voltages beyond these ratings.' bb-amp's source (350 ohm bridge, -1mV to +25mV around a 1.65V common mode per requirements.md s9a Q1/Q5) never approaches either supply rail and is inherently current-limited by the bridge's own 350 ohm - this directly supports the brief's own exclusion of protection parts at `block-only`.
decisions.source: TI INA333 datasheet s8.2.2.10 (ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina333.pdf); Analog Devices AD8237 datasheet 'Input Protection' + Fig.68 (analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8237.pdf)

layout_notes: L1. Trace symmetry: keep bridge and common-mode-resistor traces short and balanced. Source: TI TIDUB00 s5.1 - 'traces for the bridge and common mode resistors were kept as short and balanced as possible to minimize the possibility of a differential voltage in the signal chain due to trace impedance mismatch.'

L2. Gain resistor placed at the device pins, minimizing stray capacitance/trace impedance; match parasitics on both RG pins. Source: TI TIDUB00 s5.1 ('Rg was placed as close to the pins of U1 as possible'); TI INA333 datasheet s8.2.2.1 ('careful matching of any parasitics on both RG pins maintains optimal CMRR over frequency').

L3. Impedance-match both input paths, including any added source resistance, right at the in-amp pins - a mismatched path frequency response converts common-mode signal to differential. Source: Analog Devices AD8237 datasheet, Layout 'CMRR over Frequency' section.

L4. Decoupling directly at the supply pins (0.1uF), solid ground plane under the signal chain, components close to the device. Source: TI INA333 datasheet s10.1; Analog Devices AD8237 datasheet 'Power Supplies' section.

L5. REF ties to the LOCAL ground reference, not an arbitrary board ground point. Source: Analog Devices AD8237 datasheet, Layout 'Reference' subsection - 'output voltage ... is developed with respect to the potential on the reference terminal. Take care to tie REF to the appropriate local ground.'

L6. Connector/terminal-block placement should follow the common-mode-resistor connection, not the reverse. Source: TI TIDUB00 s5.1 - J1 'placed on the bottom of the PCB to allow for a close connection of R4 and R5.'

L7. If an ICF part is used, its bandwidth-mode pin (e.g. AD8237 BW) must be hard-tied to +VS as a fixed P5/P6 net (not a DNP/config strap, which is out of `block-only` scope) to achieve the 1MHz GBW this block's bandwidth math needs. Source: Analog Devices AD8237 datasheet 'Architecture' section.
errata: E1. The 'diamond plot': in-amp output swing and input common-mode voltage trade off against each other, and the usable window shrinks as supply voltage shrinks. TI INA333 s7.4.2: 'the linear common-mode input range is related to the output voltage of the complete amplifier' (Figs.20-23 plot a diamond/hexagon that visibly shrinks from 5V to 1.8V supply). Analog Devices AD8237's own cover-page Fig.2 plots a 'TRADITIONAL IN-AMP (RAIL-TO-RAIL OUT)' as a hexagon pinching to near-zero swing at common-mode extremes, against AD8237's own larger rectangle - ADI markets the ICF architecture specifically because this limitation bites hardest at low supply voltage. bb-amp's Vcm=1.65V (mid-rail on 3.3V) is the BENIGN point on this plot per requirements.md s9a; this is the correct citation for why, and remains a reviewer check on whatever gain/swing corner the final design lands in.

E2. REF pin loading (see decisions above, full detail): a classic in-amp REF driven from a bare resistor divider is a silent CMRR killer (INA333: 'tens of ohms ... noticeable degradation'); the identical mistake is a non-issue on an ICF part (AD8237: 'no effect on CMRR'). Mismatching the REF-drive assumption to the chosen architecture is the single most likely P4 schematic error on this block.

E3. Gain-resistor tolerance and tempco are NOT covered by the in-amp's own gain-error spec once the resistor is external. TI INA333: 'Gain vs temperature, G>1: +-15 to +-50 ppm/degC ... Does not include effects of external resistor RG.' TI SBOA247A design note 2: 'Low tolerance resistors must be used to minimize the offset and gain errors due to the bridge resistors.' For a 2-resistor ICF gain network, Analog Devices AD8237 'Gain Accuracy': 'two 1% resistors can cause approximately 2% maximum gain error at high gains' - ratio-match between two external parts is a worse tolerance-stacking case than a single-RG architecture unless the resistors are TCR-matched.

E4. Self-heating in the bridge and common-mode-setting resistors is a named error source in the reference vendor design, not a theoretical concern. TI SBOA247A design note 6: 'there are limitations on the current through the bridge due to self-heating effects of the bridge resistors and strain gauge.' TI TIDUB00: 'High accurate low drift resistors were used to prevent a change in resistance due to heating while handling the resistors or from self-heating due to bridge current.'

E5. Near-0V output can look deceptively 'normal' under input overload - a debugging footgun, not just a spec limit. TI INA333 s7.4.2: 'Input overload conditions can produce an output voltage that appears normal ... the output of the INA333 is near 0 V even though both inputs are overloaded.' Separately, how close to 0V the output can legitimately swing is load-dependent: INA333 gives '(V-)+0.05V typ' at RL=10k; AD8237 gives (V-)+0.05 to +0.07V at 10k tightening to +0.02 to +0.03V at 100k - both consistent with bb-amp's owner-set ~0.05-0.1V pedestal floor (requirements.md s9a Q6), and bb-amp's >100kohm output load (Q8) is the favorable case for whichever swing check P2 runs.

E6. Chopper/ALS clock feedthrough ripple applies to ICF/zero-drift parts specifically. Analog Devices AD8237 'Clock Feedthrough': internal chop clock ~27kHz; ripple 'typically 100 uV RTI when the bandwidth is greater than the clock frequency ... may be necessary to use additional filtering after the AD8237 to remove this ripple.' At G~150-165 the ~6-7kHz closed-loop bandwidth (see decisions) sits below the 27kHz clock, which should suppress most of this, but it is a part-specific check if an ICF/chopper part is the final pick, not an assumption to skip.
